essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
thinking about Sarah Perry’s article on The Limits of Epistemic Hygiene

we take germ theory so seriously, washing our hands, using antibiotics, why not meme theory?

ideas can “infect” us, linger with us, but we don’t take them seriously https://t.co/3c7RkEj4nd
Images:
- [Image #0] The image presents a slide discussing the concept of "memetic health" and its relation to the spread of ideas, drawing parallels with the spread of diseases. The slide is divided into two main sections.

The first section, titled "She outlines practices that have worked to reduce disease:", lists four key factors that have contributed to the decline of infectious diseases:
1. Improvements in nutrition
2. Cleanliness practices
3. Vaccines
4. Antimicrobial drugs

The second section, titled "And later proposes equivalents that might work to preserve memetic health within communities:", suggests four corresponding strategies for mitigating the spread of harmful ideas:
1. "Nutrition" - increasing intelligence, knowledge, and skepticism through education
2. "Cleanliness" - censorship to limit the spread of dangerous ideas; personal avoidance of sources of harmful ideas; "entertaining a thought without accepting it"
3. "Vaccines" - exposure to weakened forms of dangerous ideas
4. "Antibiotics" - helping ridicule and scorn on those who hold dangerous ideas; arguing on the internet

The text is presented in white against a dark brown background, making it easily readable.
